title: Trans rights activists protest at London Harry Potter store opening
seoTitle: London protest at Harry Potter store

tea.why: Protesters oppose the Harry Potter franchise due to author J.K. Rowling's public views on gender identity and transgender rights.
tea.want: They want to discourage public support for the franchise and raise awareness about transgender rights.
tea.changed: Nov 4: A group of demonstrators gathered outside the new flagship store on Oxford Street during its opening.

summary: On November 4, 2026, a group of transgender rights activists held a demonstration outside the opening of a new flagship Harry Potter store on Oxford Street in London. Protesters carried signs with slogans such as "protect trans lives" and "stop funding trans erasure," and used megaphones to urge fans to reconsider supporting the franchise. The action was organized to protest author J.K. Rowling's views on gender identity. While some fans ignored the protest, police were reported to be present at the scene. A spokesperson for the store stated that they support the right to peaceful expression of personal viewpoints. The demonstration coincided with the store's grand opening, which attracted a large queue of fans despite the ongoing controversy surrounding the franchise and its author.
demands: Encourage fans to stop supporting the Harry Potter franchise
response: A spokesperson for the store stated: "We support everyone’s right to the peaceful expression of personal viewpoints and look forward to a day full of magic."

crowd.text: The Standard reported a group of six people, while Variety and Rolling Stone estimated around 16 to nearly two dozen.

updates.text: Transgender rights activists gathered outside the new Harry Potter flagship store on Oxford Street to protest.
